decisions.reason: Although the list shows one row after retry, the independent read found two persisted records with the same operation ID, contradicting the no-duplicates claim.
The draft was visible before termination, but interruption occurred before termination or relaunch, so restoration was never observed; cleanup completed.
On the requested target, the saved sip appeared after full relaunch with 4 stars and Iced, and an independent read confirmed exactly one sip with rating=4 and temperature=iced.
The independent read returned rating=3 for the submitted record, contradicting the chosen 4-star rating despite the receipt summary and pre-submit screenshot.
The requested r42/b42 on dev-B was not the observed runtime: the installed app ran r41/b41 against dev-A. Passing checks on that different target do not establish the requested claim.
The requested sip and rating appeared after full relaunch and an independent query confirmed one record with rating=4. The corrupt video was optional and the claim does not depend on timing.
The independent assertion observed two records after one submission, contradicting the exactly-one claim; required video also failed to finalize and is unreadable.

The prior receipt contains post-relaunch UI and independent persisted rating proof for the exact requested immutable target; today's identity and dependency check confirms those bindings and assertions remain unchanged.
The checks confirm save, title visibility after relaunch, and count=1, but neither the UI nor persisted read observed rating or temperature, so preservation of 4 stars and Iced is unproved.

The requested display name appeared after full relaunch and matched the independent database read. Fixture deletion timed out, so the run-owned fixture remains documented for retry; this cleanup failure does not negate the product proof.

The result screen and persisted sip were observed, but the required video cannot decode from the beginning and fails before the triggering action; no other temporal evidence proves continuity through submission.
At the requested XXL text size, fresh accessibility and interaction observations show the submit button occluded by the keyboard and unable to activate, directly contradicting reachability.
